actions.action: Slice cut ends to check whether brown tissue extends into green tissue
Cut cuttings back to clean green tissue below a node with sterilized blade
Let cut ends callus in air for 1-2 days
Place cuttings in fresh water in bright indirect light and warmth, removing sphagnum
Change the water every few days
Discard any cutting that goes soft again
Lift parent plant out of pot and inspect roots
Trim rotten roots of parent with sterile scissors
Repot parent in fresh chunky aroid mix in a pot with drainage holes
Water parent only when top 2-3 inches are dry and let excess drain
Inspect base of parent plant and wounds for other rot sources

reason: The answer diagnoses stem rot instead of slow rooting, and its advice to recut the cuttings and change the water often contradicts the fix that worked (fewer water changes and patience), though it does say to remove the moss; recutting and disturbing the parent would delay rooting.
